title: Carlito's Way
about: A Puerto Rican ex-con swears he's going straight, but his old life won't let him go.
cue: Have dessert out before Benny Blanco finds Carlito at Grand Central.
faces: Grand Central, mornings. Every train out goes somewhere warmer.
I’m out of the life. Seventy-five grand put away, then the islands. Till then, eat good.
Car rental going for seventy-five. Sun every day. Come soon.
Prices subject to change. Form No. 30-5. New York, 1975.
The beach poster Carlito stares at to the last. Easy to see why.
Lacy salt cod fritters with garlic and fresh coriander.
Green plantain fried twice, smashed flat, spooned with garlic and lime mojo.
Half moon pastries of beef picadillo, olives and raisins.
Garlic and oregano pork shoulder, roasted five hours to crackling. Rice with pigeon peas.
Chicken and yellow rice, sofrito, olives, sweet peppers.
Thin sirloin under vinegar onions, white rice, red beans.
House rule: no tabs, not for nobody. Yes, Dave, that means you. Live band nightly. At the door, Pachanga.
Ringside, Saturday. Some old flames are worth the wait.
Dark rum, pineapple, fresh lime and spiced syrup, long over ice, nutmeg grated on top.
Rum, cream of coconut, pineapple, crushed ice.
Coconut caramel custard, baked slow, turned out cold.
Coconut milk pudding, cinnamon on top.

    StartersBacalaitosLacy salt cod fritters with garlic and fresh coriander.Something crisp, from El Barrio.How to make it250g salt cod200g plain flour2 tsp baking powder300ml water2 garlic cloves, crushed1 handful coriander, chopped500ml neutral oil, for fryingflaky salt, to tasteSoak the salt cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water three times, then drain and flake.Whisk the flour, baking powder, water, garlic and coriander into a loose batter and fold in the cod.Fry wide flat spoonfuls in 180°C oil in batches until golden and lacy.Drain and salt.TostonesGreen plantain fried twice, smashed flat, spooned with garlic and lime mojo.A taste of the old neighbourhood.How to make it3 green plantains500ml neutral oil, for frying3 garlic cloves, crushed2 limes, juiced60ml olive oilflaky salt, to tastePeel the plantains and cut into 3cm chunks.Fry at 160°C for 4 minutes until soft.Smash flat with a heavy glass and fry again at 190°C until crisp. Salt well.Mix the garlic, lime juice and olive oil and spoon over.MainsPernilGarlic and oregano pork shoulder, roasted five hours to crackling. Rice with pigeon peas.Seven fifty. Every bit counts toward seventy-five.How to make it2kg pork shoulder, skin on8 garlic cloves, crushed2 tsp dried oregano2 tsp salt2 tbsp white vinegar400g long grain rice400g tin pigeon peas600ml chicken stock1/2 onion, finely dicedStab the pork all over and rub with garlic, oregano, salt and vinegar. Marinate overnight in the fridge.Roast skin up at 160°C for 5 hours.Raise the oven to 230°C for 20 minutes to crackle the skin.Cook the rice with the drained pigeon peas, stock and onion until tender, and serve alongside the sliced pork.SweetsParadise flanCoconut caramel custard, baked slow, turned out cold.One last temptation.How to make it150g caster sugar395g tin condensed milk270ml coconut milk375ml evaporated milk5 eggsMelt the sugar in a pan until deep amber and pour into a ring tin.Blend the condensed milk, coconut milk, evaporated milk and eggs and pour over the caramel.Bake in a water bath at 160°C for 50 minutes until just set.Chill overnight, run a knife around the edge and turn out onto a plate.DrinksParadise punchDark rum, pineapple, fresh lime and spiced syrup, long over ice, nutmeg grated on top.Poured under the Escape to Paradise poster.How to make it50g brown sugar50ml water1 cinnamon stick180ml dark rum360ml pineapple juice60ml lime juicearomatic bitters, 4 dashes1 bag icenutmeg, freshly grated, to taste1 lime, in wheelsSimmer the sugar, water and cinnamon for 3 minutes, then cool.In a jug, stir the rum, pineapple juice, lime juice, 40ml of the syrup and bitters.Pour over ice into four tall glasses, grate nutmeg on top and garnish with a lime wheel.
